declarations.objective: Match a named set of source files against a closed taxonomy of twelve security patterns, returning one entry per match with quoted evidence, a location, a CWE, and a severity. Choose it once a change is written and the files it touched are known, to learn what the change exposes before anything depends on it. Not for judging architecture, style, or performance; not for deciding whether the change may proceed; and not for fixing what it finds.

inputs.name: security_profile
inputs.default: absent — the two patterns that depend on it are reported as not evaluated rather than as clean

inputs.name: dependency_audit
inputs.default: absent — dependency_vulnerability is reported as not evaluated rather than as clean

deterministic_behavior: the taxonomy is closed at twelve patterns, and a construct matching none of them is recorded in notes rather than in findings
a pattern whose required input was absent is listed in patterns_not_evaluated, so an unapplied pattern is never reported as clean
no path outside the supplied file set is read
findings are sorted by file then line, so two scans of one set compare directly
judgment: whether a construct matches a pattern
which severity the match carries, and what an attacker gains from it

grant.note: Read-only. The scanner produces evidence a reviewer disagrees with, and one that could edit what it flagged would leave nothing to disagree with. No shell: the boundary validator checks the result, and a guarantee a producer self-reports is not a guarantee.

failure_outcomes.reason: the file set, the scan id, or the repository root was not supplied; the producer names what is absent and returns no artifact
a path in the file set does not exist or cannot be read; scanning the rest would report a clean result over a set nobody scanned

declarations.objective: Read a captured test-run output and classify every failure into one of four causes — code, test, setup, or build — with the evidence for each and the correction it calls for. Choose it once a suite has been run and something failed, to learn what to fix before anyone edits either the code or the test. Not for running the suite, which is a script's; not for fixing what it diagnoses; and not for deciding whether the change may proceed.

inputs.name: change_under_test
inputs.default: absent — no failure is attributed to an untouched area, and the report says so

deterministic_behavior: the cause vocabulary is closed at code, test, setup, and build
one diagnosis entry exists for every failure the runner reported, and the count is carried in the artifact so a shortfall is visible
where the output shows a compile or type error before the first test result, every failure in the run is build
where no specification statement settles code against test, the cause recorded is code
the suite is not executed by this capability
judgment: which cause a failure has, given the runner's message and the code path it exercises
what correction the failure calls for

grant.note: Read-only, and it does not run the suite. Running is a script's work and its output is this capability's input, which keeps the run reproducible independently of the judgment about it.

failure_outcomes.reason: the run output, the diagnosis id, or the repository root was not supplied
the captured output holds no failure; the delegation should not have happened, and saying so is the useful answer

declarations.objective: Map every stated acceptance criterion to the test that covers it, returning one entry per criterion with the test that covers it or the reason nothing does. Choose it once tests exist and the criteria they answer to are written down, to learn which criteria are unproven while the change is still open. Not for writing tests; not for running them; not for diagnosing a failure; and not for deciding whether coverage is sufficient.
deterministic_behavior: one entry exists for every criterion supplied, including those the tests cover
the state vocabulary is closed at covered, partial, uncovered, and unauditable
no percentage, ratio, or score appears anywhere in the artifact
criteria are never derived from the implementation; only the supplied list is audited
entries are sorted by criterion identifier
judgment: whether a test would fail if the criterion stopped holding
which stated part of a criterion a test leaves unexercised

grant.note: Read-only. An auditor that could write the missing test would be proving its own finding.

failure_outcomes.reason: the criteria, the test file set, the audit id, or the repository root was not supplied
a path in the test file set does not exist; a criterion reported uncovered against a set that was not fully read is a false gap

declarations.objective: Survey the area of a codebase a stated change will touch, returning the modules already there, the conventions they follow, what must not be duplicated, and what the change risks breaking. Choose it before work is planned or written, to learn what already exists while nothing has been decided. Not for planning the change; not for judging the code's quality; not for mapping a domain model against stored knowledge, which is impact-analyst; and not for writing anything.

inputs.name: entry_points
inputs.default: absent — the area is found from the terms of the stated change, and the report says so

deterministic_behavior: every convention recorded carries a path where it can be observed
every risk recorded names at least one consumer that would notice
supplied entry points are a starting hint and never a boundary on the search
each section is sorted by path
an area where nothing exists yet returns an empty module set rather than a failure
judgment: which modules the stated change touches, depends on, or merely sits beside
what counts as an established convention rather than an incident
what already exists that the change would otherwise rebuild, and what it risks breaking

grant.note: Read-only. An inventory is what a planner argues with before committing, and a surveyor that could change the code would be describing a repository it had already altered.

failure_outcomes.reason: the stated change, the survey id, or the repository root was not supplied
the stated change names nothing the producer can find in the repository; an empty survey would read as an empty area

declarations.objective: Check each fact an implementation requires against the authored specification, returning one entry per fact stating whether the specification answers it, answers it partially, is silent, contradicts itself, or states something that cannot be built. Choose it when work has hit something the specification does not settle, before anyone decides it. Not for deciding what the specification should say; not for authoring the answer; and not for choosing whether the work proceeds.
deterministic_behavior: one entry exists for every required fact, including those the specification answers
the state vocabulary is closed at answered, partial, silent, contradictory, and infeasible
every state other than silent carries at least one exact quotation
a contradiction is recorded with both statements and is never resolved by the producer
no missing statement is drafted, and no answer is supplied for a fact the specification leaves open
entries are sorted by fact identifier
judgment: whether a specification statement settles a required fact or only bears on it
whether two statements genuinely conflict, and which of them constrains more
whether a stated requirement cannot be built, and what constraint makes it so

grant.note: Read-only, and this is the whole point. The failure this capability prevents is an implementer inventing the missing fact and shipping it as though the business had stated it; one that could write the answer would be that failure with a contract around it.

failure_outcomes.reason: the required facts, the specification set, the report id, or the repository root was not supplied
a path in the specification set does not exist; a fact reported silent across a set that was not fully read is a false gap

declarations.objective: Break a stated scope into epics and task contracts, each with one objective, its dependencies, and the criteria that decide it is done. Choose it once the scope is agreed and before any work is bound to a specification or written. Not for deciding what to build; not for binding a task to the sections its executor needs; not for estimating cost; and not for implementing.

inputs.name: existing_backlog
inputs.default: absent — nothing is checked for duplication against previously recorded work

inputs.name: specification_set
inputs.default: absent — a task's origin names the scope rather than a requirement

inputs.name: granularity_bounds
inputs.default: absent — no numeric bound is applied, and the backlog says so

deterministic_behavior: every task belongs to exactly one epic, and every epic names at least one task
task identifiers are sequential across the backlog rather than per epic
no dependency cycle is emitted; the boundary validator rejects one and the producer resolves it instead
every element of the scope that no task answers appears in open_questions
no numeric threshold is applied unless the caller supplied one
judgment: where the boundaries between epics and between tasks fall
which tasks cannot be demonstrated before which
what would show a task is done

grant.note: Read-only. A decomposer that could start building would have settled by action what the plan exists to expose.

failure_outcomes.reason: the scope, the backlog id, or the repository root was not supplied
the scope states no outcome that can be turned into a task

declarations.objective: Bind each task in a backlog to the exact specification sections its executor will need, with the version of each, the facts already established, and the inferences permitted without record. Choose it once a backlog exists and before any task is executed, so an executor reads what was chosen rather than what it finds. Not for decomposing the scope; not for deciding what a task should do; and not for executing one.

inputs.name: code_inventory
inputs.default: absent — known_context is drawn from the specification set alone

deterministic_behavior: every task in the backlog receives a binding, including one that needs nothing
no task is added, removed, merged, or re-worded
every reference carries a version, a revision identifier, or the literal unversioned
every known_context entry carries its source
a fact the specification does not settle goes to unresolved and never to known_context
judgment: which sections a task's criteria require
which established facts spare the executor a search
which inferences may be made without record

grant.note: Read-only. It chooses what an executor reads and never changes it.

failure_outcomes.reason: the backlog, the specification set, the binding id, or the repository root was not supplied
the supplied backlog does not satisfy backlog/1, so the tasks it names cannot be trusted to be the planner's

declarations.objective: Classify every external service a stated piece of work requires as available, partial, or missing, with the evidence for each and what remains before it can be relied on. Choose it before work begins that depends on a database, queue, cache, object store, or third-party service. Not for provisioning anything; not for deciding whether the work proceeds without a dependency; and not for choosing a substitute.

inputs.name: specification_set
inputs.default: absent — dependencies are derived from the stated work alone

deterministic_behavior: readiness is established by reading configuration and never by opening a connection
no setting value is read, recorded, or forwarded; only declared names are
the state vocabulary is closed at available, partial, and missing
a missing entry states what was searched
entries are sorted by dependency name
judgment: which external services the work requires, including those implied by a behavior rather than named
whether the configuration found is complete or partial

grant.note: Read-only and deliberately without a shell. Reachability from the machine that ran the check is not a fact about the repository, and foundation/0004 R18 forbids reading a secret for any reason.

failure_outcomes.reason: the work, the report id, or the repository root was not supplied

declarations.objective: Given the files a change actually modified and what changed in each, name every consumer that could break and what would break for it. Choose it after a change is written and before it is relied on, to learn what it exposes outside its own scope. Not for surveying an area before a change is planned, which is codebase-surveyor; not for judging whether the change is correct; and not for fixing anything.

inputs.name: code_inventory
inputs.default: absent — no prior risk is checked, and prior_risks_checked is empty

deterministic_behavior: the modified set is taken as stated and never derived from version control
a consumer that imports without reaching the changed behavior is not recorded as exposed
every consumer examined and cleared appears in unexposed
where a code inventory was supplied, every risk it predicted is confirmed or recorded as not realized
exposures are sorted by consumer path
judgment: whether what changed is observable outside the file
which consumers depend on the thing that changed
what breaks for each

failure_outcomes.reason: the modified set, the report id, or the repository root was not supplied
a path in the modified set does not exist, so what changed in it cannot be traced

declarations.objective: Match a named set of source files against three structural patterns that require judgement — an over-broad service, a duplicated abstraction, and a missing one — returning the evidence and what each will cost later. Choose it once a body of work is complete and its files are known. Not for the structural patterns a script decides, such as an import cycle or a layer violation; not for security; and not for deciding what work a finding becomes.

inputs.name: declared_architecture
inputs.default: absent — responsibility boundaries are drawn from what the code shows, and the scan says so

inputs.name: thresholds
inputs.default: absent — no numeric bound is applied, because this capability ships none

deterministic_behavior: the taxonomy is closed at three patterns, and the five a graph decides are out of scope
no path outside the supplied file set is read
no numeric threshold ships with this capability; every value applied is recorded with source caller or observed
findings are sorted by the first site's path
judgment: whether a class has taken on responsibilities that change for unrelated reasons
whether two implementations are the same concept
whether a repeated fragment names a concept that must stay in agreement

failure_outcomes.reason: the file set, the scan id, or the repository root was not supplied
a path in the file set does not exist; scanning the rest would report a clean structure over a set nobody scanned

declarations.objective: Review a named set of source files against the axes of a stated rule registry that require judgement — layering, dependency wiring, contract semantics, error handling, and test quality — returning one finding per departure with its evidence and cost. Choose it once a change is written and a registry exists to review it against. Not for the axes a linter decides; not for security; not for structure; and not for approving anything.
deterministic_behavior: every finding cites exactly one rule from the supplied registry
an absent registry is a stop rather than an invitation to supply one
the axis vocabulary is closed at five, and security and structure are out of scope because other capabilities hold them
every finding carries a confidence of certain or contested
findings are sorted by file then line
judgment: whether the code departs from a stated rule
what the departure costs
whether a reading of the rule could go the other way

grant.note: Read-only. A reviewer that could edit what it flagged would resolve the argument by writing.

failure_outcomes.reason: the file set, the registry, the review id, or the repository root was not supplied
a path in the file set or the registry does not exist

declarations.objective: Implement exactly one bound task contract, writing the source it requires and returning a record of what was written, what was inferred, and where the specification was departed from. Choose it once a task is bound to the material its executor needs and its dependencies are demonstrated. Not for deciding what to build; not for writing its tests; not for running anything; and not for taking a second task.
deterministic_behavior: exactly one task is implemented per delegation
no file outside the task is changed; what should change is recorded in deferred instead
every criterion of the task appears in criteria_addressed, satisfied or not
every inference the binding did not permit appears in inferences
an unresolved fact bearing on the task is a stop, and nothing is written
nothing is executed: no build, no test, no version control operation
judgment: how to satisfy the criteria with the material the binding supplied
whether a needed fact is settled by the references or is a gap

grant.note: The only write grant in this set, and bounded by the absence of a shell: running is a script's work under foundation/0004 R6, and an implementer that could run its own tests would be the sole witness to whether its work passed.

failure_outcomes.reason: the task, the binding, the record id, or the repository root was not supplied

declarations.objective: Write the tests for one implemented task — one per acceptance criterion plus the edge cases its kind requires — and return a record of what each test proves and what was left untested. Choose it once a task is implemented and its criteria are known. Not for implementing the task; not for running the suite; not for auditing coverage; and not for judging whether the implementation is correct.

inputs.name: reproduction
inputs.default: required for a task of kind defect and absent otherwise; without it a regression test tests the fix rather than the defect

deterministic_behavior: every test written records what would make it fail
a task of kind restructure receives no new behavioral test; an uncovered restructured area is recorded in untested
a task of kind defect without a reproduction is a stop
every edge case considered and dismissed appears in not_applicable with its reason
the implementation is never changed, including where the author believes it is wrong
nothing is executed
judgment: what proves a criterion
which edge cases the task's kind requires
which inferences in the implementation record need pinning

grant.note: Writes tests and nothing else. No shell: a test the author watched pass is a test the author would stop reading.

failure_outcomes.reason: the task, its criteria, the implementation record, the record id, or the repository root was not supplied
a task of kind defect arrived without the failure it fixes

declarations.objective: Turn a stated scope into a reviewable plan: survey what exists, break the scope into tasks, bind each task to the specification sections its executor needs, and report what the specification leaves open and what infrastructure is missing. inputs.name: specification_set
inputs.default: absent — a task's origin names the scope, and binding produces references to nothing

inputs.name: existing_backlog
inputs.default: absent — nothing is checked for duplication against recorded work

deterministic_behavior: survey, decompose and bind run in that order and are never reordered
no state is recorded and no run is resumed; a second invocation starts over
an artifact that fails its contract at the boundary is carried to the person rather than repaired
the gap pass runs only where a binding recorded an unresolved entry, and its absence is reported
no granularity threshold is supplied to the decomposer unless the caller gave one
the run ends at the plan and starts no work

how to summarize the plan for the person reading it

nothing is executed: no build, no test, no version control operation
no state is recorded and no run is resumed
no readiness or approval is asserted over the work produced
